answer: A registered amateur astronomy observatory anchors identity to one place and a nightly log: the society registers one observatory per member, records its coordinates and requires dated logs. A comet of fake observatories founders because each needs a real telescope, a dark-sky site, and months of dated logs. The horizon is the log's cross-check: the same sky events must appear in the logs of neighbouring observatories on the same night. A zephyr of forged logs, invented observations, fails that cross-check, so the attacker must run a real observatory per identity, about $2,000 each.
